name: job_postings
description: Job postings from a European tech job board. Each record is one open position.
context: Postings come from startups, scale-ups and enterprises across Europe. Annual gross salaries (EUR) depend mainly on seniority, then on location (Zurich, London, Munich and Amsterdam pay more; Lisbon, Warsaw and Bucharest less) and on department (engineering and data pay above marketing and people). Required skills are concrete technologies and practices that match the title and seniority: juniors list fundamentals, seniors list architecture, mentoring and specific platforms. Remote roles are common in engineering and rare in sales. Descriptions read like real postings: company pitch, responsibilities, requirements, benefits; tone varies by company type.

fields.name: job_title
fields.description: Job position title, specific rather than generic (e.g. 'Senior Backend Engineer, Payments').

fields.name: salary
fields.description: Annual gross base salary in EUR (midpoint of the advertised band), consistent with seniority, location and department.

fields.name: skills
fields.description: Required skills/technologies matching the title and seniority.

rules: Salary bands by seniority (EUR): intern 30-40k, junior 35-55k, mid 50-80k, senior 70-115k, lead 90-150k, principal 120-200k; shift up ~25% for CH/UK and down ~30% for PL/RO/PT.
years_experience_min fits seniority: intern 0, junior 0-2, mid 2-5, senior 5-8, lead 7-12, principal 10+.
The city is a real city in the country; remote roles still name the company's home city.
The description mentions the title, the remote policy and several of the listed skills.
checks: len({s.lower() for s in skills}) == len(skills)

diversity.scenario_guidance: Vary company type (seed startup, scale-up, bank, agency, public sector, NGO), industry, team situation (new team, rebuild, growth, backfill) and role focus.
